subject: MQM Function - Interval Estimates of QTL Location

messages.author: 567c476eb6fe219c
messages.subject: MQM Function - Interval Estimates of QTL Location
parts:
I am a new user of r-QTL trying to get to grips with the MQM functions.

I understand how to run mqmscan and get a LOD score profile. However, I do not understand how to extract the relevant gene intervals from the profile.

I know I can run mqmprocesspermutation or mqmscanfdr to get probability or false discovery rate information about the peaks in the profile. However, I am not sure what to do then.

Should I be looking only at the LOD profile from mqmscan, or should I use fitqtl and refineqtl to get the QTL locations from the result of mqmgetmodel?

Assuming I am looking only at the LOD profile - single-QTL mapping only investigates the highest peak in the profile. Since this is multiple QTL mapping, do I look at *all* the peaks with an adequate probability/false discovery rate? Is there a way to calculate LOD support intervals/Bayes credible intervals for multiple peaks?

Thanks for any help,
Stephanie

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] MQM Function - Interval Estimates of QTL Location
parts:
Personally, if I see evidence for multiple QTL, I prefer to bring them together into a joint multi-QTL model, using makeqtl, fitqtl, refineqtl, ...

There's not currently an easy way to calculate LOD support or Bayes credible intervals in a single-QTL scan with multiple peaks on a chromosome, though you can subset the results to a portion of the chromosome. I wouldn't trust this, though; I'd want to look at a multi-QTL model.

Here's an example:

data(hyper)
hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper, step=1)
out <- scanone(hyper)

bayesint(out[out$chr==1 & out$pos<60,])
# chr pos lod
# D1Mit19 1 37.2 2.944148
# c1.loc45 1 48.3 3.529452
# c1.loc50 1 53.3 2.498271

bayesint(out[out$chr==1 & out$pos>60,])
# chr pos lod
# c1.loc62 1 65.3 2.584748
# c1.loc75 1 78.3 3.476983
# c1.loc80 1 83.3 2.675915

karl
